@graph.headline: Free Token Listing and Press Release Sites: Worth It in 2026?
@graph.alternativeHeadline: The honest operator's read on free crypto listing and PR sites: what they do, where they hurt, and what actually moves a token launch
@graph.description: Free token listing and press release sites give your project basic discoverability and mild SEO value. They are not a PR campaign. This 2026 breakdown covers which directories are worth using, where free sites quietly damage credibility, and what a real token listing PR campaign looks like from narrative through TGE day.

itemListElement.name: Free Token Listing and Press Release Sites: Worth It in 2026?

mainEntity.name: Are free token listing sites worth using for a launch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, for the mechanical step of getting your project indexed, but not as a PR strategy. CoinMarketCap and CoinGecko are essential and free; they are directory listings, not PR tools. Free press release distribution sites provide mild SEO value and basic indexation. None of them generate journalist coverage, move investor perception, or build the narrative that makes a token launch land. Use them in an hour, then direct your attention and budget to earned media. The full launch sequence is in the pre-token launch PR checklist at shilikajain.com/playbook/pre-token-launch-pr-checklist.

mainEntity.name: What is a token listing PR campaign?

acceptedAnswer.text: A token listing PR campaign is the full communications arc from narrative development through TGE day through post-launch cadence, built to move investor and journalist perception rather than just get a project name on a directory. It includes a clear narrative brief, targeted outreach to tier-1 outlets like CoinDesk, Cointelegraph, Decrypt and The Block, a structured exclusive or embargo for the announcement itself, and a post-launch content cadence. Free listing sites are a small mechanical element of the broader campaign, not the campaign itself.

mainEntity.name: How much does a proper token launch PR campaign cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A launch sprint typically runs $15,000 to $40,000 for a defined campaign window around the TGE. A fractional senior PR operator working on the launch on a monthly basis runs $5,000 to $12,000 per month. Full agency rates start at $15,000 and go to $45,000 per month. Free listing sites cost nothing, but the budget that actually moves a launch goes toward earned media strategy, pitch execution, and press materials, not directory submissions.

mainEntity.name: Which paid PR distribution services are worth it for a crypto token launch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Chainwire's premium tier and GlobeNewsWire are the most commonly used for crypto, at roughly $500 to $3,000 per release depending on the package. They provide indexation breadth and a citable record on partner sites. They are supplements to earned media, not replacements for it. If the budget is constrained, earned media outreach to five specific journalists beats paid wire distribution every time, because one real placement in CoinDesk is worth more to investor credibility than fifty wire pickups.

mainEntity.name: What does a TGE comms plan actually look like?

acceptedAnswer.text: A TGE comms plan runs in four phases: narrative build four to six weeks before the launch, the announcement itself structured as an exclusive or embargoed drop to tier-1 outlets, listing day broad-channel communications, and a post-launch monthly cadence. Free sites are relevant only in the listing day phase. The other three phases require earned media strategy and execution. The full structure is in the TGE comms plan glossary at shilikajain.com/glossary/what-is-a-tge-comms-plan.
